```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern context-budget
 * @options dad22f213e339fb5
 */

/**
 * Fitting a conversation into a model's context window.
 *
 * The newest turns that fit, with everything older folded into a summary.
 *
 * The arithmetic is the part worth reading. A context window holds the request
 * and the reply together, so the room for the answer comes off before anything
 * is measured — a conversation weighed against the whole window fits right up
 * to the moment the model tries to answer. Two other costs are not messages and
 * are as easy to forget: the system prompt, which this port sends as a field
 * rather than a turn, and the tool schemas, which go with every request.
 *
 * Each message is its own unit here. A conversation carrying tool results needs
 * the pairing rule instead — dropping an assistant turn while keeping the
 * results that answer it produces a request every provider rejects, and this
 * file has no role to put those results in.
 *
 * Nothing here shortens a message. A truncated question is a different
 * question, so a conversation whose undroppable part is larger than the window
 * is refused rather than trimmed into one that fits.
 */

/**
 * The conversation, as the `chat-model-port` pattern's messages.
 *
 * Declared here rather than imported, so this file depends on nothing. It is
 * the same shape, which the emitted type tests state as a claim in both
 * directions: a conversation from the port can be measured, and what comes back
 * can be sent.
 *
 * There is no `system` role, because the port has none — a system prompt is a
 * field on the request. That is not a detail here: it makes the system prompt
 * the one piece of context that cannot be dropped, so it is measured as a fixed
 * cost rather than considered as a candidate.
 */

/**
 * A run of text.
 */
export interface TextPart {
  readonly type: "text";
  readonly text: string;
}

/**
 * What the caller said.
 */
export interface UserMessage {
  readonly role: "user";
  readonly content: readonly TextPart[];
}

/**
 * What the model said.
 */
export interface AssistantMessage {
  readonly role: "assistant";
  readonly content: readonly TextPart[];
}

export type Message = UserMessage | AssistantMessage;

/**
 * What has to fit, and what it has to fit into.
 *
 * Every number is in tokens, and every one of them describes the same request:
 * the window the provider allows, and the parts of that window this
 * conversation does not get to use.
 */

export interface Budget {
  /** The provider's window for this model, request and reply together. */
  readonly contextWindow: number;
  /**
   * Room to leave for the answer. Taken off the window before anything is
   * measured. Left out, a conversation is fitted against room the reply needs,
   * and the request is rejected on the way back rather than on the way out.
   */
  readonly reserveForOutput: number;
  /**
   * Room to leave for the summary, taken off before the turns to summarise are
   * chosen. A summary written into room measured after the choice overflows the
   * request by its own size. A summariser that comes back with more than this
   * is refused rather than sent. Any number above zero also charges one
   * message's framing, because the summary travels in the system field and a
   * request with no system prompt has not paid for that field yet.
   */
  readonly reserveForSummary: number;
  /**
   * What the dropped turns become. Given every message that was dropped, in
   * order. Usually another model call, which is why it may return a promise. It
   * is called only when something was actually dropped, so a conversation that
   * fits costs nothing.
   */
  readonly summarise: (dropped: readonly Message[]) => string | Promise<string>;
  /**
   * The system prompt, which is a field on a request rather than a message in
   * it. Measured here so a caller cannot forget it, and charged one message's
   * framing: one mainstream wire format sends it as the first message, and
   * paying for framing it does not have is the harmless direction to be wrong
   * in.
   */
  readonly system?: string;
  /**
   * What the provider adds around each message: the role, the delimiters, the
   * turn markers. A per-provider fudge factor, and small — but a conversation
   * of eighty short turns is mostly framing, so leaving it out is how a window
   * that was measured carefully still overflows.
   */
  readonly perMessageOverhead?: number;
  /**
   * How to count tokens. The provider's own tokeniser, where there is one. The
   * default is an estimate and is documented as one. Anything sized close to
   * the window wants the real thing.
   */
  readonly countTokens?: (text: string) => number;
}

/**
 * A conversation that fits, and what it cost.
 *
 * `system` is the prompt to send, with the summary folded in. It is here rather
 * than in a field a caller has to remember to read, because a summary that is
 * produced and then left behind is the one failure this strategy cannot report:
 * the request is valid, in budget, and missing everything the model was told
 * about the conversation so far.
 */
export interface Fitted {
  readonly kind: "fitted";
  /** The conversation to send, in order. */
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  /**
   * What was left out, in order. Worth logging: it is the context the model
   * will not have.
   */
  readonly dropped: readonly Message[];
  /**
   * The system prompt to send, which is the caller's with the summary folded
   * into it.
   */
  readonly system: string;
  /**
   * What the request will cost: the kept messages and the system prompt with
   * its summary. `tokens + reserveForOutput` never exceeds `contextWindow`,
   * which is the invariant worth asserting in a caller's own suite.
   */
  readonly tokens: number;
}

/**
 * What cannot be dropped does not fit.
 *
 * Both numbers are in the same currency, which is the input side of the window:
 * `available` is the window less the room the reply was promised, and `needed`
 * is what the request costs with every droppable turn already gone.
 */
export interface Overflow {
  readonly kind: "overflow";
  readonly needed: number;
  readonly available: number;
}

/**
 * Either a conversation to send or the refusal to shorten a question.
 */
export type Budgeted = Fitted | Overflow;

/**
 * Fits a conversation into a budget, or says that it cannot be done.
 *
 * The newest turns that fit, with everything older folded into a summary.
 *
 * Returns the `overflow` arm when what cannot be dropped does not fit. Nothing
 * is truncated to avoid that: a shortened question is a different question.
 *
 * Send both halves of the result. The messages alone are in budget and missing
 * what the summary was written to carry.
 */
export async function fitToBudget(
  messages: readonly Message[],
  budget: Budget,
): Promise<Budgeted> {
  const count = budget.countTokens ?? estimateTokens;
  const overhead = budget.perMessageOverhead ?? MESSAGE_OVERHEAD;

  // The reply's room comes off first. A window holds both halves of the
  // exchange, so a conversation measured against the whole of it fits until the
  // moment the model tries to answer.
  const available = budget.contextWindow - budget.reserveForOutput;

  // And these are charged before anything is chosen, because nothing below can
  // drop them: the system prompt is a field rather than a turn. The field's
  // framing is charged whenever a summary has room to appear, because the
  // summary travels in that same field. Charged afterwards instead, a
  // conversation with no system prompt overflows by the framing of a field its
  // own summary brought into being.
  const framed = budget.system !== undefined || budget.reserveForSummary > 0;
  const fixed =
    (framed ? overhead : 0) +
    (budget.system === undefined ? 0 : count(budget.system));

  // Nothing is droppable at this point, so this is the answer rather than a
  // special case of one.
  if (fixed > available) {
    return refused(fixed, available);
  }

  const units = unitsOf(messages).map((unit): Unit => ({
    messages: unit,
    tokens: unit.reduce(
      (total, message) => total + costOf(message, count, overhead),
      0,
    ),
  }));

  const chosen = select(units, available - fixed);

  if (chosen.kind === "over") {
    return refused(fixed + chosen.needed, available);
  }

  // Nothing was dropped, so there is nothing to summarise and no reason to pay
  // a model to say so. The reserve is left unspent rather than spent on an
  // empty summary.
  if (chosen.dropped.length === 0) {
    return fitted(chosen, fixed, budget.system ?? "");
  }

  // The summary's room comes out of the conversation's *before* the turns to
  // summarise are chosen. Measured after, the request is over budget by the
  // size of the summary that was supposed to bring it under.
  const shorter = select(units, available - fixed - budget.reserveForSummary);

  if (shorter.kind === "over") {
    return refused(
      fixed + budget.reserveForSummary + shorter.needed,
      available,
    );
  }

  const summary = await budget.summarise(shorter.dropped);
  const written = count(summary);

  // A summariser that overran its room is refused rather than sent. The
  // alternative is a request that overflows by however far it overran, which
  // the provider reports and this file could not.
  if (written > budget.reserveForSummary) {
    return refused(fixed + written + shorter.tokens, available);
  }

  return fitted(shorter, fixed + written, withSummary(budget.system, summary));
}

/**
 * The chosen turns, with the costs that are not turns added back in.
 */
function fitted(chosen: Chosen, fixed: number, system: string): Fitted {
  return {
    kind: "fitted",
    messages: chosen.messages,
    dropped: chosen.dropped,
    system,
    tokens: fixed + chosen.tokens,
  };
}

/**
 * The summary, in front of the prompt it belongs to.
 *
 * In the system prompt rather than in a message, because this port has no role
 * for it: as a user turn it is something the user never said, and as an
 * assistant turn it is something the model never said. One mainstream format
 * sends the system prompt as the first message anyway, which is where a summary
 * would have gone by hand.
 */
function withSummary(system: string | undefined, summary: string): string {
  return system === undefined ? summary : `${system}\n\n${summary}`;
}

/**
 * Choosing which turns to send.
 */

/**
 * One message, weighed.
 */
interface Unit {
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  readonly tokens: number;
}

/**
 * The turns that fit, or the size of the ones that have to.
 *
 * `over` carries only what is needed, because the room it did not fit in is
 * whatever the caller passed. Discriminated by a string rather than by a
 * boolean: a boolean discriminant stops narrowing in a project with
 * `strictNullChecks` off, which is one of the strictness settings this file is
 * expected to compile under.
 */
type Chosen = {
  readonly kind: "chosen";
  readonly messages: readonly Message[];
  readonly dropped: readonly Message[];
  readonly tokens: number;
};

type Selection = Chosen | { readonly kind: "over"; readonly needed: number };

/**
 * Fills `room` with turns, newest first.
 *
 * The newest turn is pinned: it is the question, and a request without it asks
 * nothing. Everything else is offered from the newest backwards and the search
 * stops at the first turn that does not fit, rather than stepping over it to
 * reach a smaller one behind it. A conversation with a hole in it reads as
 * though those turns never happened, which is worse than one fewer turn and
 * harder to notice.
 */
function select(units: readonly Unit[], room: number): Selection {
  const newest = units.at(-1);

  if (newest === undefined) {
    return { kind: "chosen", messages: [], dropped: [], tokens: 0 };
  }

  if (newest.tokens > room) {
    return { kind: "over", needed: newest.tokens };
  }

  const keep = new Set<Unit>([newest]);
  const older = units.slice(0, -1);
  let left = room - newest.tokens;

  for (const unit of [...older].reverse()) {
    if (unit.tokens > left) break;

    keep.add(unit);
    left -= unit.tokens;
  }

  // One mainstream format requires the first message to be the user's, and a
  // window that opens part-way through an exchange reads oddly to any model.
  // The newest unit is exempt: a tool loop asking for an answer to results it
  // has just produced has nothing else to send.
  for (const unit of units) {
    if (!keep.has(unit)) continue;
    if (unit === newest || beginsWithUser(unit)) break;

    keep.delete(unit);
  }

  const kept = units.filter((unit) => keep.has(unit));

  return {
    kind: "chosen",
    messages: kept.flatMap((unit) => unit.messages),
    dropped: units
      .filter((unit) => !keep.has(unit))
      .flatMap((unit) => unit.messages),
    tokens: kept.reduce((total, unit) => total + unit.tokens, 0),
  };
}

/**
 * Whether a unit opens with the caller speaking.
 */
function beginsWithUser(unit: Unit): boolean {
  return unit.messages.at(0)?.role === "user";
}

/**
 * Groups the conversation into units that are kept or dropped whole.
 *
 * One message each, because without tool results there is nothing in a
 * conversation that has to travel with something else. The shape is kept so
 * that the pairing rule is a change to this function alone.
 */
function unitsOf(
  messages: readonly Message[],
): readonly (readonly Message[])[] {
  return messages.map((message) => [message]);
}

/**
 * What a message costs.
 */

/**
 * What one message costs: its framing, plus what its content serialises to.
 */
function costOf(
  message: Message,
  count: (text: string) => number,
  overhead: number,
): number {
  return message.content.reduce(
    (total, part) => total + count(part.text),
    overhead,
  );
}

/**
 * What the provider adds around each message, when a caller has not said.
 *
 * Small, and it is the kind of small that adds up: a conversation of eighty
 * short turns is mostly framing. The real figure is in the provider's own
 * documentation and is worth looking up.
 */
const MESSAGE_OVERHEAD = 4;

/**
 * Characters per token, for the default estimate.
 *
 * An English-prose figure. Code runs denser than prose, and a language written
 * without spaces runs much denser — CJK text is close to one token per
 * character, where this is out by a factor of four in the direction that fails.
 */
const CHARACTERS_PER_TOKEN = 4;

/**
 * Roughly how many tokens some text will cost.
 *
 * Rounded up, deliberately. An estimate that guesses low causes exactly the
 * rejection this file exists to prevent, and one that guesses high costs a turn
 * of context.
 *
 * It is an estimate, and for anything sized close to the window it is the wrong
 * tool: pass the provider's own tokeniser as `countTokens` and this is never
 * called.
 */
export function estimateTokens(text: string): number {
  return Math.ceil(text.length / CHARACTERS_PER_TOKEN);
}

/**
 * Reports a conversation whose undroppable part does not fit.
 *
 * One function, called from each place that can discover it, so that what a
 * refusal carries is decided once. Nothing here shortens anything to avoid the
 * refusal: what cannot be dropped is the system prompt and the newest turn, and
 * a shortened version of either is a different request from the one the caller
 * made.
 */
function refused(needed: number, available: number): Overflow {
  return { kind: "overflow", needed, available };
}
```

## context-budget-example.ts (example)

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern context-budget
 * @options dad22f213e339fb5
 */

/**
 * A support chat that has outgrown its window.
 *
 * Two calls. The first has to lose turns and shows which ones; the second is a
 * question that does not fit on its own, which is the case nothing can rescue.
 */

import { fitToBudget } from "./context-budget.js";
import type {
  AssistantMessage,
  Budget,
  Message,
  UserMessage,
} from "./context-budget.js";

/**
 * The conversation so far, and the two constructors it is written with.
 */

function said(text: string): UserMessage {
  return { role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text }] };
}

function replied(text: string): AssistantMessage {
  return { role: "assistant", content: [{ type: "text", text }] };
}

/**
 * Six messages, oldest first.
 */
const CHAT: readonly Message[] = [
  said("hello, I am chasing an order from last week"),
  replied("happy to help. do you have the order number?"),
  said("it is A-1041, placed on the tuesday"),
  replied("that one shipped on wednesday and is due friday"),
  said("is there a tracking number for it?"),
  replied("there is: TRK-88213, on the courier's site"),
  said("and can I change the delivery address now?"),
];

/**
 * Long enough that no window in this file could hold it.
 */
const LOG = "GET /orders/A-1041 200 OK\n".repeat(40);

/**
 * The window this model has, and everything in it that the conversation does
 * not get.
 *
 * No `countTokens`, so the default estimate is used — fine for an example and
 * not for a request sized close to the edge, where the provider's own tokeniser
 * is the only honest answer.
 */
const BUDGET: Budget = {
  contextWindow: 160,
  reserveForOutput: 60,
  system: "You are a support agent. Be brief and never guess an order status.",
  reserveForSummary: 24,
  // Normally a call to a cheap model. Kept as a function here so the example
  // has no network in it, and it is worth noticing that it must come back
  // inside the room reserved above.
  summarise: (dropped: readonly Message[]): string =>
    `Earlier: ${String(dropped.length)} turns about order A-1041.`,
};

/**
 * Fitting the chat, then failing to fit a question.
 *
 * Both halves of the result are sent: the messages alone are in budget and have
 * lost everything the summary was written to carry.
 */
export async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const fitted = await fitToBudget(CHAT, BUDGET);

  if (fitted.kind === "overflow") {
    report(
      `the chat needs ${String(fitted.needed)} tokens and has ${String(fitted.available)}`,
    );

    return;
  }

  report(
    `kept ${String(fitted.messages.length)} of ${String(CHAT.length)} messages ` +
      `for ${String(fitted.tokens)} tokens, dropping ${String(fitted.dropped.length)}`,
  );

  report(`the prompt to send is now: ${fitted.system}`);

  // The other case: a question that does not fit on its own. Nothing can be
  // dropped to make room for it, and shortening it would answer a question
  // nobody asked.
  const essay = [said(`here is the whole log: ${LOG}`)];

  const refused = await fitToBudget(essay, BUDGET);

  if (refused.kind === "overflow") {
    report(
      `refused: it needs ${String(refused.needed)} tokens and has ${String(refused.available)}`,
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Where the example's output goes.
 */
function report(message: string): void {
  console.log(message);
}
```

## context-budget.test-d.ts (test)

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern context-budget
 * @options dad22f213e339fb5
 */

/**
 * The claims about this file's conversation that no suite which runs could
 * check.
 *
 * Two of them are about fitting into the `chat-model-port` pattern, which is
 * where a conversation comes from and where the fitted one goes. A file that
 * had drifted out of shape with the port would behave identically here and fail
 * at the call site, so the port's messages are declared below and compared
 * rather than described in a comment.
 */

import type { Budget, Budgeted, Message } from "./context-budget.js";

/**
 * Forces its argument to be `true`, and fails to compile when it is not.
 *
 * Each assertion below is written as a named alias rather than a bare one, so
 * that it reads as a stated claim about the code and cannot be mistaken for a
 * leftover.
 */
export type Expect<T extends true> = T;

/**
 * Whether `X` is assignable to `Y`.
 *
 * Both sides are wrapped in a tuple to stop the union distribution a bare
 * conditional performs. Undistributed is the question that was meant: whether
 * the whole of `X` is acceptable as a `Y`, rather than whether each member of
 * it is on its own.
 */
export type Extends<X, Y> = [X] extends [Y] ? true : false;

/**
 * Whether `X` is rejected where a `Y` is wanted.
 *
 * The type-level counterpart to `@ts-expect-error`, and preferable wherever the
 * claim is about a relationship rather than about a particular line: a
 * directive suppresses whichever error occurs, so it can be satisfied by an
 * unrelated mistake on the same line, where this cannot.
 */
export type NotAssignable<X, Y> = [X] extends [Y] ? false : true;

/**
 * The port's conversation, written out so that the comparison is a claim and
 * not a hope.
 *
 * `failed` is on the port's result and not on this file's, which is why these
 * are compared by assignability rather than by identity: a file that measures
 * messages needs the fields that cost something and no others.
 */
interface PortText {
  readonly type: "text";
  readonly text: string;
}

interface PortCall {
  readonly type: "tool-call";
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  readonly input: unknown;
}

interface PortResult {
  readonly type: "tool-result";
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  readonly output: unknown;
  readonly failed?: boolean;
}

type PortMessage =
  | { readonly role: "user"; readonly content: readonly PortText[] }
  | {
      readonly role: "assistant";
      readonly content: readonly (PortText | PortCall)[];
    }
  | { readonly role: "tool"; readonly content: readonly PortResult[] };

/**
 * What comes back can be sent: the fitted conversation is the port's.
 */
export type FittedIsSendable = Expect<
  Extends<readonly Message[], readonly PortMessage[]>
>;

/**
 * The port's conversation is refused, which is what turning the pairing rule
 * off means.
 *
 * Not a shortcoming: without the rule this file cannot promise that a tool call
 * and its results stay together, so it declines to be given any. Stated as a
 * relationship rather than with a directive, which would be satisfied by any
 * error on the line.
 */
export type PortIsRefused = Expect<
  NotAssignable<readonly PortMessage[], readonly Message[]>
>;

/**
 * A refusal carries no conversation, so a caller cannot send one without
 * looking first.
 *
 * The point of the union rather than an empty message list: an unchecked result
 * whose messages are `[]` sends a request with no conversation in it, which
 * most providers answer.
 */
export function overflowHasNoMessages(result: Budgeted): number {
  // @ts-expect-error the overflow arm has no messages on it
  return result.messages.length;
}

/**
 * A budget with no summariser is refused, rather than being one that drops the
 * turns instead.
 *
 * The field has no default for that reason. What a default would buy is a
 * budget that compiles and does something other than what the strategy is for.
 */
export function theStrategyNeedsItsOwnFields(): Budget {
  // @ts-expect-error a summarising budget has to say what to summarise with
  return {
    contextWindow: 8192,
    reserveForOutput: 1024,
    reserveForSummary: 256,
  };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern context-budget
 * @options dad22f213e339fb5
 */

/**
 * The arithmetic, exactly.
 *
 * Every case counts one token per character and turns the framing charge off,
 * so the numbers here are arithmetic rather than approximation — which is the
 * only way to tell a budget that forgot the reply's room from one that did not,
 * since both fit.
 *
 * What is being pinned is mostly what a conversation loses. A window that
 * measures against the whole of itself is right until the model answers; a turn
 * stepped over leaves a hole nothing reports; a summary measured after the
 * choice overflows by its own size. None of those announce themselves at the
 * call site.
 */

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { estimateTokens, fitToBudget } from "./context-budget.js";
import type {
  AssistantMessage,
  Budget,
  Fitted,
  Message,
  Overflow,
  UserMessage,
} from "./context-budget.js";

/**
 * A conversation, a budget that charges only what a case asks it to, and two
 * ways to read a result.
 */

/**
 * One token per character.
 *
 * An exact counter rather than the estimate, so that a case can say what a
 * conversation costs instead of roughly what it costs. Real ones are the
 * provider's, and are not this simple.
 */
function perCharacter(text: string): number {
  return text.length;
}

/**
 * A budget with every default turned off, which each case adds to.
 *
 * The framing charge is zero here so that the numbers below are the messages
 * and nothing else. A real budget leaves it on: turning it off is how a
 * conversation of many short turns comes out a third under its true size.
 */
const EXACT: Budget = {
  contextWindow: 100,
  reserveForOutput: 0,
  reserveForSummary: 0,
  summarise: (): string => "",
  perMessageOverhead: 0,
  countTokens: perCharacter,
};

/**
 * The same budget with the defaults left in: the estimate and the framing
 * charge.
 */
const ESTIMATED: Budget = {
  contextWindow: 100,
  reserveForOutput: 0,
  reserveForSummary: 0,
  summarise: (): string => "",
};

/**
 * The turns a case is written from.
 */
function said(text: string): UserMessage {
  return { role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text }] };
}

function replied(text: string): AssistantMessage {
  return { role: "assistant", content: [{ type: "text", text }] };
}

/**
 * Five turns of four tokens each, which is the conversation most cases below
 * are cut from.
 */
const CHAT: readonly Message[] = [
  said("aaaa"),
  replied("bbbb"),
  said("cccc"),
  replied("dddd"),
  said("eeee"),
];

/**
 * Each message as a short label, so a case can name the turns that survived in
 * one assertion.
 */
function labelsOf(messages: readonly Message[]): readonly string[] {
  return messages.map(labelOf);
}

function labelOf(message: Message): string {
  return message.content.map((part) => part.text).join(" ");
}

/**
 * The conversation that fitted, or a failure naming what came back instead.
 *
 * Every case below is about the arithmetic rather than about unwrapping a
 * union, so the unwrapping happens once, here.
 */
async function fit(
  messages: readonly Message[],
  budget: Budget,
): Promise<Fitted> {
  const result = await fitToBudget(messages, budget);

  if (result.kind === "overflow") {
    throw new Error(
      `expected a fit, got an overflow needing ${String(result.needed)}`,
    );
  }

  return result;
}

/**
 * And the refusal, however this file reports one.
 */
async function refusalOf(
  messages: readonly Message[],
  budget: Budget,
): Promise<Overflow> {
  const result = await fitToBudget(messages, budget);

  if (result.kind !== "overflow") {
    throw new Error(
      `expected an overflow, got a fit costing ${String(result.tokens)}`,
    );
  }

  return result;
}

describe("the arithmetic", () => {
  it("keeps everything when everything fits", async () => {
    const fitted = await fit(CHAT, EXACT);

    expect(labelsOf(fitted.messages)).toEqual([
      "aaaa",
      "bbbb",
      "cccc",
      "dddd",
      "eeee",
    ]);
    expect(fitted.dropped).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(fitted.tokens).toBe(20);
  });

  it("takes the reply's room out of the window before measuring", async () => {
    const roomy = await fit(CHAT, { ...EXACT, contextWindow: 20 });
    const cramped = await fit(CHAT, {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 20,
      reserveForOutput: 16,
    });

    // The same conversation against the same window. All that changed is what
    // was promised to the answer, and a budget that leaves it out fits until
    // the model tries to use it.
    expect(roomy.messages).toHaveLength(5);
    expect(labelsOf(cramped.messages)).toEqual(["eeee"]);
  });

  it("counts the system prompt, which is a field rather than a turn", async () => {
    const bare = await fit(CHAT, { ...EXACT, contextWindow: 20 });
    const prompted = await fit(CHAT, {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 20,
      system: "ssssssssssssssss",
    });

    expect(bare.messages).toHaveLength(5);
    expect(labelsOf(prompted.messages)).toEqual(["eeee"]);
    expect(prompted.tokens).toBe(20);
  });

  it("charges the system prompt one message's framing too", async () => {
    const framed = await fit([said("aaaa")], {
      ...EXACT,
      perMessageOverhead: 3,
      system: "ssss",
    });

    // Two lots of framing for one turn and one prompt. The prompt is a field
    // rather than a message, but one mainstream format puts it on the wire as
    // the first message, and paying for framing it may not have is the harmless
    // direction to be wrong in.
    expect(framed.tokens).toBe(14);
  });

  it("charges the framing the provider puts around each message", async () => {
    const bare = await fit(CHAT, EXACT);
    const framed = await fit(CHAT, { ...EXACT, perMessageOverhead: 10 });

    expect(bare.tokens).toBe(20);
    expect(framed.tokens).toBe(70);
  });

  it("reports a total the reply still fits beside", async () => {
    const budget: Budget = {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 32,
      reserveForOutput: 8,
      system: "ssss",
    };
    const fitted = await fit(CHAT, budget);

    // 24 of the window is the input's, and the whole conversation and the
    // prompt come to exactly that. `tokens + reserveForOutput ===
    // contextWindow` is the invariant worth asserting in a caller's own suite,
    // and this is the edge of it.
    expect(fitted.messages).toHaveLength(5);
    expect(fitted.tokens).toBe(24);
  });
});

describe("choosing which turns to send", () => {
  it("keeps the newest turns and drops the oldest", async () => {
    const fitted = await fit(CHAT, { ...EXACT, contextWindow: 12 });

    expect(labelsOf(fitted.messages)).toEqual(["cccc", "dddd", "eeee"]);
    expect(labelsOf(fitted.dropped)).toEqual(["aaaa", "bbbb"]);
  });

  it("stops at a turn that does not fit instead of stepping over it", async () => {
    const chat = [said("aa"), replied("d".repeat(40)), said("bb")];
    const fitted = await fit(chat, { ...EXACT, contextWindow: 10 });

    // "aa" would have fitted in what was left. Taking it would send two turns
    // that read as consecutive with forty tokens of exchange missing between
    // them, which is a worse answer than one turn fewer and a quieter one.
    expect(labelsOf(fitted.messages)).toEqual(["bb"]);
    expect(fitted.dropped).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it("does not open the window with the model speaking", async () => {
    const chat = [said("aaaa"), replied("bb"), said("cc")];
    const fitted = await fit(chat, { ...EXACT, contextWindow: 6 });

    // There was room for the model's turn, and it goes anyway: one mainstream
    // format rejects a conversation that opens with an answer to a question it
    // cannot see.
    expect(labelsOf(fitted.messages)).toEqual(["cc"]);
    expect(labelsOf(fitted.dropped)).toEqual(["aaaa", "bb"]);
  });

  it("sends the newest turn even when it is not the caller's", async () => {
    const fitted = await fit([replied("aaaa")], EXACT);

    // The exemption to the rule above. A loop asking for an answer to what it
    // has just produced has nothing else to send, and trimming this would leave
    // a request with no conversation in it.
    expect(labelsOf(fitted.messages)).toEqual(["aaaa"]);
  });

  it("fits an empty conversation", async () => {
    const fitted = await fit([], EXACT);

    expect(fitted.messages).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(fitted.tokens).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe("what cannot be made to fit", () => {
  it("refuses a question larger than the window", async () => {
    const refusal = await refusalOf([said("a".repeat(50))], {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 20,
    });

    // Not truncated to fit. A shortened question is a different question, and
    // an answer to it is worse than a refusal because it looks like an answer.
    expect(refusal.needed).toBe(50);
    expect(refusal.available).toBe(20);
  });

  it("counts the promise to the answer in what there was room for", async () => {
    const refusal = await refusalOf([said("a".repeat(50))], {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 20,
      reserveForOutput: 5,
    });

    expect(refusal.available).toBe(15);
  });

  it("counts the system prompt in what was needed", async () => {
    const refusal = await refusalOf([said("a".repeat(50))], {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 20,
      system: "ssss",
    });

    // The prompt cannot be dropped either, so the smallest this request could
    // become is both of them.
    expect(refusal.needed).toBe(54);
  });

  it("refuses a system prompt larger than the window on its own", async () => {
    const refusal = await refusalOf([], {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 4,
      system: "ssssssss",
    });

    // Nothing is droppable here, so there is no conversation to shorten and no
    // arithmetic to do.
    expect(refusal.needed).toBe(8);
    expect(refusal.available).toBe(4);
  });
});

describe("the summary", () => {
  it("is given exactly what was dropped, once", async () => {
    let seen: readonly Message[] | undefined;
    let calls = 0;
    const fitted = await fit(CHAT, {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 12,
      // Enough room reserved that the summary costs the conversation a turn, so
      // what was dropped for the summary to describe is not what would have
      // been dropped without it.
      reserveForSummary: 4,
      summarise: (dropped: readonly Message[]): string => {
        seen = dropped;
        calls += 1;

        return "";
      },
    });

    expect(calls).toBe(1);
    expect(labelsOf(seen ?? [])).toEqual(labelsOf(fitted.dropped));
  });

  it("is not written when nothing was dropped", async () => {
    let calls = 0;
    const fitted = await fit([said("aa")], {
      ...EXACT,
      summarise: (): string => {
        calls += 1;

        return "a summary of nothing";
      },
    });

    // A conversation that fits costs nothing, which is worth more than it
    // sounds: a summariser is usually another model call, and one per request
    // that did not need it is a bill.
    expect(calls).toBe(0);
    expect(fitted.system).toBe("");
  });

  it("has its room taken out before the turns are chosen", async () => {
    const budget: Budget = {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 14,
      summarise: (): string => "ss",
    };
    const generous = await fit(CHAT, { ...budget, reserveForSummary: 2 });
    const stingy = await fit(CHAT, { ...budget, reserveForSummary: 6 });

    expect(labelsOf(generous.messages)).toEqual(["cccc", "dddd", "eeee"]);

    // Four more tokens promised to the summary, and a turn comes out of the
    // conversation to pay for it. Reserved after the choice instead, the
    // request would be over budget by the size of the summary that was meant to
    // bring it under.
    expect(labelsOf(stingy.messages)).toEqual(["eeee"]);
  });

  it("goes in front of the caller's prompt", async () => {
    const fitted = await fit(CHAT, {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 20,
      system: "be brief",
      reserveForSummary: 4,
      summarise: (): string => "gist",
    });

    expect(fitted.system).toBe("be brief\n\ngist");

    // And it is paid for: the prompt, the summary and the one turn that was
    // left room.
    expect(fitted.tokens).toBe(16);
  });

  it("pays for the field it puts itself in", async () => {
    // Three turns from one speaker, so what is chosen below is decided by the
    // arithmetic rather than by which speaker the window happens to open on.
    const asked = [said("aaaa"), said("bbbb"), said("cccc")];
    const fitted = await fit(asked, {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 12,
      perMessageOverhead: 1,
      reserveForSummary: 2,
      summarise: (): string => "ss",
    });

    // There is no system prompt here, so nothing has paid for that field's
    // framing — and the summary is what brings the field into being. Charged on
    // the way out instead, two turns and a summary come to exactly the window
    // and arrive one token over it.
    expect(labelsOf(fitted.messages)).toEqual(["cccc"]);
    expect(fitted.tokens).toBe(8);
  });

  it("is refused when it overran the room reserved for it", async () => {
    const refusal = await refusalOf(CHAT, {
      ...EXACT,
      contextWindow: 12,
      reserveForSummary: 4,
      summarise: (): string => "x".repeat(40),
    });

    // Sending it would put the request over by however far the summariser
    // overran — reported by the provider, from a stack that has nothing to do
    // with the summary.
    expect(refusal.needed).toBe(44);
  });
});

describe("the default estimate", () => {
  it("rounds up", () => {
    // Guessing low causes exactly the rejection this file exists to prevent.
    // Guessing high costs a turn of context, which is the affordable direction.
    expect(estimateTokens("abcde")).toBe(2);
    expect(estimateTokens("")).toBe(0);
  });

  it("is what a budget with no counter of its own uses", async () => {
    const fitted = await fit([said("a".repeat(40))], ESTIMATED);

    // Forty characters is ten tokens, and the framing this budget left switched
    // on is four more.
    expect(fitted.tokens).toBe(14);
  });
});
```
